name: Nuclear risk
value: No US–Russia treaty limits; satellite warning
summary: Western intelligence reportedly expects a Russian nuclear-armed satellite launch as soon as December; Kremlin denies it
state: German media (NDR, WDR, Süddeutsche Zeitung) reported on 23 Nov that NATO intelligence believes Russia is ready to launch a nuclear-armed satellite, possibly in December; Russia's embassy in Germany and Kremlin spokesman Peskov called the reports unfounded (Reuters via US News; AeroTime, 24 Nov). No US–Russia treaty limits apply since New START lapsed. No nuclear test, alert-level change or threatened use in an active conflict was found to 24 Nov, so Watch holds on the arms-control lapse.
for_you: There is no change to public safety advice; in the UK, follow official government emergency guidance. A nuclear detonation in orbit would chiefly threaten satellites that support navigation, communications and weather services.
rubric_hit: Watch: arms-control lapse without replacement (no New START limits) and reported preparations for a nuclear-armed satellite

sources.title: US News (Reuters) — NATO believes Russia is ready to launch nuclear-armed satellite, German media say
AeroTime — Russia may launch a nuclear-armed satellite by year-end, German media report

why: Nuclear use anywhere would be a civilisational shock; arms-control treaties are weaker than at any time since the 1960s.
drivers: Threats in active wars, testing, doctrine changes, arms-control collapse, proliferation.

rubric.alert: A nuclear test, changes in deployment/alert levels, or threatened use in an active conflict.
rubric.watch: Explicit threats, unusual exercises, doctrine changes, or arms-control lapses without replacement.
rubric.normal: No explicit nuclear threats or tests; arms-control dialogue active.
